questions.q: After joining WIN-SRV-04 to the Servers OU with the CIS-based GPO baseline linked, which command confirms which policies actually applied to that machine?
options: gpresult /r
manage-bde -on C:
auditpol /set /subcategory:"Logon"
sysmon64.exe -i baseline-config.xml
questions.explain: gpresult /r shows exactly which GPOs applied to this machine and in what order, which is what goes in the change ticket as proof.

questions.q: Why do WIN-SRV-04's Private and Public firewall profiles have no custom rules written for them at all?
options: Because this server will never legitimately find itself on either network type, so default deny-all-inbound is itself the correct control
Because Windows Firewall doesn't support rules on those profiles
Because those profiles only matter for laptops, never servers
Because the Domain profile rules automatically apply to all three profiles
questions.explain: An unused profile left at default deny is a deliberate hardening decision, not an oversight — the server only ever operates on the Domain profile.

questions.q: What does running `manage-bde -protectors -adbackup C:` accomplish that enabling BitLocker alone does not?
options: It escrows the recovery key to the computer's object in Active Directory so it's retrievable even if the disk fails
It disables BitLocker on the C: drive
It forces a full disk re-encryption
It replaces the recovery password with a PIN
questions.explain: Without the AD backup step, the recovery key only exists locally or on paper — adbackup is what makes it recoverable from a failed disk.

questions.q: Why does this lab enable specific audit subcategories like "Security State Change" rather than the old legacy audit categories?
options: Granular subcategories generate the Event IDs that matter without flooding the Security log with noise the SOC won't read
Legacy categories are no longer supported in any version of Windows
Subcategories require less disk space than categories
There's no functional difference between the two approaches
questions.explain: The all-or-nothing legacy categories generate far more noise than the targeted subcategory settings this lesson configures.

questions.q: What does deploying Sysmon add that Windows' native event logging doesn't already provide?
options: Deeper visibility such as process creation, network connection, and file creation events, written to their own operational log
A replacement for the Windows Firewall
Automatic patch deployment
BitLocker key management
questions.explain: Native logging stops at "a process ran" — Sysmon's Event IDs 1, 3, and 11 fill in the detail native Windows auditing doesn't capture.
